note: Each statement describes the communication students can do at that grade. A linked skill is a place to see it in the studio. Teachers can read the earlier statements to find prerequisite literacy demands without repeating a lower grade's whole unit.

strands.title: Explaining mathematical thinking
strands.about: How students communicate what they did and why.

grades.statement: Describe what was counted.
Explain an addition strategy.
Describe an array and its equation.
Compare multiplication strategies.
Justify a fraction operation.
Explain a proportional relationship.
Defend a solution using mathematical evidence.
Construct and critique a mathematical argument.

strands.title: Mathematical vocabulary
strands.about: From naming objects to using precise, contrastive terms.

grades.statement: Name numbers, shapes and positions with pictures.
Use place-value and measurement words in context.
Tell mathematical meanings from everyday meanings (product, table).
Use word parts and cognates (numerator, equivalent).
Use precise terms for operations and models (expression, volume).
Distinguish related terms (ratio, rate, percent).
Use terms to build definitions and critique them.
Use technical language across representations (function, slope, congruent).

strands.title: Reading mathematical situations
strands.about: From picture stories to multi-quantity situations with unstated relationships.

grades.statement: Read a short story and say what happened.
Find the question and the numbers in a two-step story.
Name what is known and unknown in an equal-groups situation.
Read multiplicative comparison language without keyword shortcuts.
Read multi-step situations with fractions and decimals.
Read rate and ratio language and identify the relationship.
Read conditional language and unstated relationships.
Read multi-part modeling situations and state assumptions.

strands.title: Interpreting data
strands.about: From counting categories to reasoning about association and inference.

grades.statement: Sort and count objects into categories.
Read picture graphs and bar graphs.
Read scaled graphs and measurement data.
Read line plots with fractions.
Use line plots and the mean to interpret data.
Describe a distribution's shape, center and spread.
Use a sample to make an inference.
Describe association in a scatter plot and use a line of best fit.

strands.title: Mathematical writing
strands.about: From labelled drawings to evidence-based arguments.

grades.statement: Draw and label, then write one number sentence.
Write a sentence that tells the strategy.
Write an explanation with a because sentence.
Write to compare two methods.
Write a justification for a calculation with fractions.
Write a because, but and so explanation about a ratio.
Write a paragraph with claim, evidence and reasoning.
Write and revise a mathematical argument.

strands.title: Speaking and discussion
strands.about: From sharing an answer to defending and questioning reasoning.

grades.statement: Say what you counted to a partner.
Explain a strategy to a partner.
Ask and answer questions about an array.
Agree or disagree with a strategy and say why.
Respond to a partner's reasoning with a question.
Defend a ratio claim with a table.
Critique a classmate's argument politely and precisely.
Lead a discussion that compares models.

strands.title: Listening comprehension
strands.about: From following one-step directions to evaluating spoken arguments.

grades.statement: Follow one-step directions with a picture.
Follow two-step directions.
Listen to a situation and name the quantities.
Match a spoken strategy to a model.
Hear a spoken explanation and spot the first error.
Listen for the relationship in a spoken ratio situation.
Evaluate a spoken argument for evidence.
Compare spoken explanations of a model and critique them.

strands.title: Representation
strands.about: From objects and pictures to tables, graphs, equations and models.

grades.statement: Connect objects, pictures and numerals.
Connect tens and ones models to numbers.
Connect an array to a multiplication statement.
Connect fraction models to number lines.
Connect a coordinate pair to a situation.
Connect a ratio table to a double number line.
Compare table, graph, equation and description.
Move among function representations.

strands.title: Mathematical modeling
strands.about: From acting out a story to building and testing a model with limits.

grades.statement: Act out and draw a simple situation.
Use a bar model for a two-step story.
Write an equation for a situation.
Choose an operation structure for a multistep situation.
Model a situation with fractions and decimals.
Model a situation with a ratio or an equation.
Build a proportional model and state its limits.
Build, test and defend a linear model.

strands.title: Argumentation
strands.about: From giving an answer to proving a claim and handling counterexamples.

grades.statement: Say whether two groups are equal and show how.
Say which is greater and give a reason.
Say whether a property always works and test examples.
Check a claim with a counterexample.
Justify why multiplying can make a number smaller.
Justify that two ratios are equivalent.
Defend a conclusion using mathematical evidence.
Construct and critique an argument with a counterexample.
